source_text: Infibulation, involving narrowing of the vaginal opening through stitching or other means, constitutes nearly 80% of cases, often accompanied by reinfibulation after childbirth to restore tightness, while less severe Type I (sunna) forms are reported but frequently overstated, masking underlying mutilation upon clinical examination. [2]
